Jacob Marley was dead, and he had been dead for seven years. <break time="0.8s" /> His business partner, Ebenezer Scrooge, was a man who loved only money. <break time="0.8s" /> He was as hard and sharp as flint, and his heart was as cold as ice. <break time="0.8s" /> On Christmas Eve, Scrooge sat busy in his counting house, and it was bitterly cold. <break time="0.8s" /> His clerk, Bob Cratchit, worked in a tiny room with a very small fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Bob tried to warm himself at his candle, but he failed. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Scrooges nephew Fred came in and cheerfully wished him a merry Christmas. <break time="0.8s" /> Bah, Humbug, said Scrooge, and he refused to come to Christmas dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Next, two gentlemen visited the office to collect money for the poor. <break time="0.8s" /> Are there no prisons, asked Scrooge, Those who are poor must go there. <break time="0.8s" /> If they would rather die, they had better do it, he said coldly. <break time="0.8s" /> At closing time, Scrooge grumbled that Bob wanted the whole day off for Christmas.

제이컵 말리는 죽었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그가 죽은 지 7년이 되었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 동업자. <break time="0.8s" /> 에버니저 스크루지는. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 돈만 사랑하는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 부싯돌처럼 단단하고 날카로웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그의 마음은 얼음처럼 차가웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 크리스마스 이브에. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지는 바쁘게 앉아 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 사무실에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 날이 지독하게 추웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 서기 밥 크래칫은. <break time="0.8s" /> 비좁은 방에서 일했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아주 작은 불 하나만 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 밥은 몸을 녹이려고 애썼다. <break time="0.8s" /> 촛불에 하지만 실패했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그때 스크루지의 조카 프레드가 들어왔다 그리고 쾌활하게 그에게 빌어 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 즐거운 크리스마스를. <break time="0.8s" /> 흥, 허튼소리, 스크루지가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그는 거절했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 크리스마스 저녁 식사에 오는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 다음으로 신사 두 명이 사무실을 찾아왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 가난한 사람들을 위한 돈을 모으려고. <break time="0.8s" /> 감옥이 없단 말이오. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지가 물었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 가난한 사람들은. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리로 가야 하오. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들이 차라리 죽겠다면. <break time="0.8s" /> 그렇게 하는 게 낫겠지. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 차갑게 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 문 닫을 시간에. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지는 투덜거렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 밥이 하루를 통째로 쉬려 한다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 크리스마스에.

That night. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge saw Marleys face. <break time="0.8s" /> In the knocker on his front door. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked again. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was only a knocker. <break time="0.8s" /> So he went inside. <break time="0.8s" /> Later as he sat by his small fire. <break time="0.8s" /> He heard a loud clanking noise. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Marleys ghost came straight. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the heavy door. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was still locked. <break time="0.8s" /> The ghost dragged a long chain. <break time="0.8s" /> That was made of cash boxes, keys, and heavy purses. <break time="0.8s" /> I wear the chain. <break time="0.8s" /> I forged in life. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the ghost. <break time="0.8s" /> I made it link by link. <break time="0.8s" /> Because I cared only about money. <break time="0.8s" /> But you were always a good man of business. <break time="0.8s" /> Jacob said Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> Mankind was my business. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried the ghost. <break time="0.8s" /> Wringing its hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Marley warned that Scrooges own chain. <break time="0.8s" /> Was even longer and heavier than his. <break time="0.8s" /> Three Spirits will visit you. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> They are your only hope. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the ghost floated out. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And Scrooge fell asleep at once.

그날 밤. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지는 말리의 얼굴을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 집 현관문의 문고리에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 다시 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 그것은 그냥 문고리였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그는 안으로 들어갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 나중에 그가 작은 난롯불 옆에 앉아 있을 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 요란하게 쩔그럭거리는 소리를 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러더니 말리의 유령이 곧장 들어왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 무거운 문을 뚫고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 문은 여전히 잠겨 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 유령은 긴 쇠사슬을 끌고 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 사슬은 돈궤, 열쇠, 무거운 지갑으로 만들어져 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 나는 사슬을 차고 있다네. <break time="0.8s" /> 살아 있을 때 내가 만든. <break time="0.8s" /> 유령이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 나는 그것을 고리 하나하나 만들었지. <break time="0.8s" /> 돈에만 관심을 두었기 때문이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 자네는 늘 훌륭한 사업가였잖나. <break time="0.8s" /> 제이컵 스크루지가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들이 바로 내가 돌봐야 할 일이었어. <break time="0.8s" /> 유령이 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 손을 비틀며. <break time="0.8s" /> 말리는 경고했다 스크루지 자신의 사슬이. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 것보다 훨씬 더 길고 무겁다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 세 유령이 자네를 찾아갈 걸세. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들이 자네의 유일한 희망이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러고 나서 유령은 둥실 떠나갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 창문을 통해. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 스크루지는 곧바로 잠이 들었다.

When the bell struck one. <break time="0.8s" /> The first spirit appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> Beside Scrooges bed. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a strange figure. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a child and an old man. <break time="0.8s" /> At the same time. <break time="0.8s" /> A bright, clear light shone. <break time="0.8s" /> From the top of its head. <break time="0.8s" /> I am the Ghost of Christmas Past. <break time="0.8s" /> It said. <break time="0.8s" /> Your past. <break time="0.8s" /> The spirit took him back. <break time="0.8s" /> To the school where he had spent lonely Christmases as a boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge saw his younger self. <break time="0.8s" /> Reading alone. <break time="0.8s" /> And he began to cry. <break time="0.8s" /> Next, they visited old Mister Fezziwig. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had been Scrooges kind master. <break time="0.8s" /> Fezziwig gave a happy Christmas party. <break time="0.8s" /> And everyone danced until eleven oclock. <break time="0.8s" /> The happiness he gives. <break time="0.8s" /> Is as great as if it cost a fortune. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Scrooge saw a young woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Belle. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had once loved him. <break time="0.8s" /> She said that a golden idol, money. <break time="0.8s" /> Had taken her place in his heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Show me no more. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> For he could not bear to watch.

종이 한 시를 치자. <break time="0.8s" /> 첫 번째 유령이 나타났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지의 침대 옆에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것은 이상한 모습이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아이 같기도 하고 노인 같기도 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 동시에. <break time="0.8s" /> 밝고 맑은 빛이 빛났다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것의 머리 꼭대기에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 나는 지나간 크리스마스의 유령이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 바로 너의 과거 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 유령은 그를 다시 데려갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 학교로 그곳에서 그는 어린 시절 외로운 크리스마스를 보냈었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지는 어린 자신을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 혼자 책을 읽고 있는 모습을. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그는 울기 시작했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 다음으로 그들은 늙은 페지윅 씨를 찾아갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 스크루지의 친절한 주인이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 페지윅 씨는 즐거운 크리스마스 파티를 열었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 모두가 열한 시까지 춤을 추었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그분이 주는 행복은. <break time="0.8s" /> 큰돈을 들인 것만큼이나 크지. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그다음 스크루지는 한 젊은 여인을 보았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 벨이라는 이름의. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 한때 그를 사랑했었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 말했다 황금 우상, 곧 돈이. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 마음속 자기 자리를 차지했다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 더는 보여 주지 마시오. <break time="0.8s" /> 스크루지가 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 차마 지켜볼 수 없었기 때문이다.

The second spirit was a jolly giant. <break time="0.8s" /> In a green robe. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding a glowing torch. <break time="0.8s" /> He took Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> To the small house of his clerk, Bob Cratchit. <break time="0.8s" /> Bob earned only fifteen shillings a week. <break time="0.8s" /> But his family was full of joy. <break time="0.8s" /> They shared a small goose and a pudding. <break time="0.8s" /> And nobody said. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was small. <break time="0.8s" /> Bobs little son, Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a weak boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Who walked with a crutch. <break time="0.8s" /> God bless us, every one. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> At the end of dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Spirit, tell me. <break time="0.8s" /> If Tiny Tim will live. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Scrooge with new interest. <break time="0.8s" /> If these shadows stay the same. <break time="0.8s" /> The child will die. <break time="0.8s" /> Answered the spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the spirit repeated. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooges own cold words. <break time="0.8s" /> And Scrooge hung his head in shame. <break time="0.8s" /> Next they visited Freds merry party. <break time="0.8s" /> Where everyone was laughing and playing games. <break time="0.8s" /> Fred felt sorry for his uncle. <break time="0.8s" /> Because Scrooge only hurt himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge enjoyed the games so much. <break time="0.8s" /> That he begged to stay longer.
